assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Table columns represent public inputs and observable outputs, not internal state.
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Applicant Type | Age | Claim Count | Status? | Premium?

assertions.text: No column named after private fields or internal variables.
assertions.evidence: Columns used: 'Applicant Type', 'Age', 'Claim Count', 'Status?', 'Premium?' — no riskScore or hasActivePolicy column.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language, not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: "Scenario | Applicant Type | Age | Claim Count | Status?  | Premium?"

assertions.text: Scenario names name the condition, not the result.
assertions.evidence: "Renewal, no claims, would otherwise be standard" paired with AUTO_APPROVED — names condition, not outcome.

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Premium?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Status?, Premium?, Status?, Premium?, Premium?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 3 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 3 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern.
assertions.evidence: Three @TableTest methods: autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims, rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold, calculatesPremiumByAgeTier.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed, no re-covering of rules.
assertions.evidence: calculatesPremiumByAgeTier rows 3-4 ('Well below threshold, no claims'=106, 'Well above threshold, no claims'=231.50) re-cover the same senior tier-switch already shown by rows 1-2, instead of covering the stated claim-impact obligation.

assertions.text: Decision logic and premium calculation are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims and rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold tables both assert Status? and Premium? together: "assertEquals(status, result.decision()); assertEquals(premium, result.premium(), 0.001);"

assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas.
assertions.evidence: "EvaluationResult result = evaluator.evaluateApplication(applicantType, age, claimCount); assertEquals(status, result.decision());" — no arithmetic in body.

assertions.text: @Description explains business context, not internal formulas.
assertions.evidence: "Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15. Applications are rejected once the score exceeds 75."

assertions.text: Decision table covers the 4 vs 5 claims rejection cliff regardless of age.
assertions.evidence: Table2 uses age 9 vs 10 with fixed claims=5 to hit exact risk score 75/76, with no row testing 4 claims at all, contrary to the required claims-based cliff.

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: the premium jump from 0 to 1 claim (impact of +15 risk score on premium), and the premium difference at age 64 vs 65 (standard vs senior formula). These boundary conditions document how premium changes at each threshold.
assertions.evidence: calculatesPremiumByAgeTier rows are 64/1,65/1,30/0,90/0 - no 0-vs-1 claim pair at a fixed age within this table

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Status?/Premium? values vary across rows in every table, e.g. 'APPROVED' vs 'REJECTED' vs 'AUTO_APPROVED' and premiums 106.00/136.00/142.00/273.50

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Description states 'Risk score is age/10 + claimCount * 15... rejected once the score exceeds 75' and '100 + riskScore * 2.0 below age 65, and 200 + riskScore * 3.5 from age 65 onward'

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or the method name it falls back to) states what the code under test does.
assertions.evidence: Method names: 'autoApprovesRenewalsWithNoClaims', 'rejectsApplicationsAboveRiskThreshold', 'calculatesPremiumByAgeTier' all describe system actions

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: The generated tests pass when executed against InsuranceEvaluator
assertions.evidence: Tests passed

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description.
assertions.evidence: "Applicant type does not affect premium... so it is held fixed at NEW here." explicitly declares the held constant

assertions.text: A comparison criterion applied by the assertion must be stated on the published surface.
assertions.evidence: assertEquals(premium, result.premium(), 0.001) uses only a conventional floating-point epsilon, exempted from this rule
